chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who is on the Day of Arafah, and between him and Mecca are three miles, and he is performing Tamattu' (Umrah to Hajj). He said: He cuts off the Talbiyah of Tamattu' and invokes Allah for Hajj with the Talbiyah when he prays Fajr, and proceeds to Arafat, so he stands with the people, and completes all the rituals, and stays in Mecca until he performs Umrah al-Muhrim, and there is nothing upon him.
Do you not see that he directed the address in the first report to one who feared missing the standing (at Arafah), and in the second report to one who is between him and Mecca three miles?
And it is known that one in this situation cannot enter Mecca and engage in Ihlal (changing from Ihram to Umrah) and Ihram (re-entering Ihram for Hajj) while catching up with the people at Arafah.
And whenever he cannot do that, his obligation is to continue in his current Ihram and make it a Hajj, according to what we mentioned.

And whoever forgets the Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah with Hajj until he arrives at Arafah, let him remember there what he says at the time of Ihram. If he does not remember until he returns to his country, then his Hajj is complete and there is nothing upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفُ: Al-Mawqif (the standing at Arafah, a pillar of Hajj)
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ الْمُحَرَّمِ: Umrah al-Muhrim (the Umrah performed by those in the state of Ihram for Hajj, specifically in the context of Tamattu')
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who cannot return to Mecca to perform Umrah on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of the *Tamattu'* Hajj structure, specifically addressing the scenario where a pilgrim is too distant from Mecca to perform *Umrah al-Muhrim* before the Arafah stand. It establishes that converting the existing Umrah Ihram into Hajj Ihram on the spot is sufficient, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations when logistical constraints arise. The text further extends this leniency to cases of forgetfulness regarding the initial Ihram declaration, emphasizing that the core act of standing at Arafah remains the pivotal moment of validity.
